metric.capability_efficiency.basis: all-fragments (single-language shard; common-basis recomputation deferred to runner aggregation once all 10 language shards are merged)
blockers: No live toolchain execution was available in this packet-only worker; all support levels, fragment shapes and complexity counts are derived from the Zig language reference and std library documentation rather than an executed build/run under the frozen recipe. This is recorded as an evidentiary limitation, not a fabricated pass: V1 (build/run match) evidence for these 44 Zig fragments still needs mechanical toolchain execution before the run's Semantic Compression status can be marked COMPLETE.

Cross-language normalization of Capability Efficiency to a true 0-100 comparability scale requires the other nine languages' raw_E figures, which are outside this shard's assignment; the provisional score above must be superseded at aggregation.

categories: syntax_forms: count of distinct syntactic constructs (keywords/operators/builtin calls/type forms) that must appear in the Zig fragment to express and correctly interpret the probe's canonical_task, counted once per distinct construct actually used in the measured_fragment.

context_dependent_rules: count of rules whose meaning at the site depends on surrounding context (target type, build/safety mode, comptime vs runtime, memory-ordering parameter, etc.) rather than being fixed by local syntax alone.

implicit_rules: count of behaviors that occur at the site without being written explicitly in the fragment (compiler-inserted bounds checks, monomorphization, implicit ABI assignment from `export`, duck-typed generic constraints not stated at declaration, hidden aliasing through pass-by-value structs containing pointers, etc.).

documented_exceptions: count of Zig-language-reference-documented special-case behaviors that deviate from the 'plain' rule for that construct (e.g. signed-overflow trap under -OReleaseSafe vs silent UB under -OReleaseFast; @rem sign-of-dividend vs @mod exception; safety-checked indexing UB).
frozen_counting_rule.itemization_requirement: Every probe's four sub-counts are itemized individually in probe_evidence[] below so the total is auditable and no category defaults to 0 by omission; a category with truly zero occurrences for that probe is recorded as 0 with the reasoning implicit in the fragment shape, never left blank.
frozen_counting_rule.unknown_vs_zero: No category was recorded 'unknown' for Zig: the Zig language reference and std library documentation were available for every probe reasoned about here, so 0 always means 'no such rule applies', not 'undocumented'.

probe_evidence.fragment_note: const n: i32 = 7; return n; — literal 7 (comptime_int) coerces to i32 by context.
var counter: i64 = 0; const LIMIT: i64 = 100; — module-scope var default lifetime is program lifetime (implicit).
var v: i32 = undefined; if/else assigns both arms; reading undefined before assignment is safety-checked UB (documented exception).
var buf: [16]u8 = undefined; genuinely uninitialized, not zero-filled.
x += 1; overflow traps under -OReleaseSafe (frozen recipe), UB under fast mode (exception).
xs.items[1] = 42; compiler-inserted bounds check is implicit.
&slot pointer, port.* = 9, return slot.
window: []const i32 = xs.items[0..3]; slice is a non-owning fat pointer (implicit representation fact).
allocator.create(Foo) + try, ArrayList(*Foo) round-trip, pointer equality `first == second` is genuine identity test.
f(x) bare call; ArrayList passed by value still aliases underlying buffer through its internal pointer field (hidden aliasing).
put(cell: *i32) { cell.* = 12; } called as put(&cell); fully explicit.
fn mid(xs) i32 { return xs[1]; } — i32 result is an independent value copy, unambiguous.
anonymous tuple return .{q,r}; destructuring `const q, const r = divmod2(a,b);` (Zig tuple destructuring).
r = a*b+c; overflow trap behavior implicit per operand type, documented exception under fast mode.
@divTrunc, @rem, @floatFromInt x2; @rem sign-of-dividend vs @mod is a documented exception.
std.math.add(i32,m,1) catch 0 — rung(i) checked error-union op.
std.math.divTrunc(i32,a,b) catch 0 — rung(i) checked op.
std.mem.eql(u8,s1,s2) — explicit contents comparison.
std.mem.sort(i32,xs,{},std.sort.desc(i32)) in-place; a<b comparison.
std.math.cast(i32,big) orelse 0 — rung(i) optional-returning cast.
@as(f64,@floatFromInt(i)) + d — Zig forbids implicit int/float mixing, conversion fully explicit.
xs[i] — compiler-inserted bounds check implicit; traps under ReleaseSafe (documented exception vs ReleaseFast UB).
xs[1..4] slice shares storage with xs (implicit representation fact).
?i32 optional type, null literal, orelse fallback.
Substituted explicit `if (o) |v| h(v) else null` (P-a); no optional-map operator in std.
fn parse_twice(s) !i32 { const v = try std.fmt.parseInt(i32,s,10); return v*2; }
std.fmt.parseInt(i32,s,10) catch 0.
union(enum){Circle:struct{r:f64},Rect:struct{w:f64,h:f64}}; closed set.
switch(s){.Circle=>|c|...,.Rect=>|r|...} — exhaustiveness enforced implicitly by compiler.
Manual vtable substitute: anyopaque ptr + fn-pointer field, @ptrCast to recover concrete type (unsafe, implicit trust).
fn head(xs: anytype) @TypeOf(xs[0]) { return xs[0]; } — monomorphized per call site (implicit codegen).
comptime T param with `>` used in body; constraint checked only at instantiation, not declared (P-c).
Same manual-vtable substitute as F14.P3 used to hold heterogeneous concrete types behind one abstract element type.
std.ArrayList(i32) + appendSlice(try) + explicit for-loop sum (no generic fold in std for arbitrary iterables).
std.StringHashMap(i32): put/try, iterator()/while-next, get orelse; iteration order unspecified (documented); resize allocation implicit on put.
openFile/try, defer file.close(), readToEndAlloc/try, return len.
defer h.deinit() manually invoked; no compiler-guaranteed automatic destructor (P-c).
@import("std"); std.debug.print("x\n",.{});
pub fn pub_add / private fn secret in util.zig; @import("util.zig").pub_add(2,3) from outside.
std.Thread.spawn x2 (try), .join() x2, sum results — real OS-thread concurrency shipped in std.
std.atomic.Value(i64).fetchAdd(1,.monotonic) from two threads; memory-ordering argument is context-dependent.
@cImport(@cInclude("stdlib.h")).abs(-3) — C ABI assumed implicitly by @cImport.
export fn add2(a:c_int,b:c_int) c_int {return a+b;} — export implies C ABI+unmangled symbol implicitly.

raw_calculation.normalization_formula_used: score = min(100, round(100 / raw_E)) — a self-consistent, monotonically-decreasing-in-E transform applied per language shard because this worker cannot see the other nine languages' raw_E values needed for a proper cross-language min-max normalization. THIS FIGURE IS PROVISIONAL: the runner must recompute the final 0-100 Capability Efficiency score for every language from the merged set of raw_E values once all language shards are aggregated, per spec 6.1.4.E and the interaction_with_quality_metrics basis-reporting requirement.

partial_citations.F12.P2: P-c/P-a: Zig std library provides `orelse`/`.?` for optionals but no map/andThen-style optional-preserving chaining operation; the substitute uses an explicit `if (o) |v| ... else null` payload-capture conditional, which is the R9-permitted substitution the probe names.
partial_citations.F14.P3: P-a: Zig unions/enums are closed at their declaration; there is no interface/protocol type for retroactive external conformance. Extensibility from a separate unit is approximated only via a hand-written vtable (struct of `*anyopaque` + function pointers), a weaker, more verbose standard idiom, not a native open-dispatch mechanism.
partial_citations.F15.P2: P-c: Zig comptime generics (`comptime T: type`) use structural/duck-typed constraint checking performed only at instantiation; there is no declaration-site constraint syntax, so the documented guarantee the probe asks for (constraint stated at declaration) is unavailable.
partial_citations.F15.P3: P-a: same vtable substitute as F14.P3 is required to hold two concrete types behind one abstract element type with runtime dispatch, since Zig has no interface type.
partial_citations.F17.P2: P-c: Zig has no compiler-invoked destructor/drop; `deinit()` is a library convention that must be invoked manually, here via `defer h.deinit()`, which is a scoped-construct substitute the rubric explicitly permits, not a guaranteed automatic end-of-lifetime hook.
